text.p: Securities research group Merrill Lynch downgraded shares of Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem to "reduce" from "neutral" in a company update dated August 13.
"Borsodchem's first half earnings were slightly disappointing and our full-year target may prove challening," Merrill Lynch said.

Borsodchem reported an 1997 first half IAS after-tax profit of 3.62 billion forints compared with 3.36 billion in the same period of 1996, on net sales of 29.6 billion forints compared with 21.33 billion in the first half of 1996.
"We have seen margins decline at Borsodchem for two reasons, first the higher cost of raw materials...and secondly margin pressure in German mark exports," Merrill Lynch said.
The Hungarian market advanced 54 percent in dollar terms this year while Borsodchem's price increased 56 percent over the same period, Merrill Lynch said.

It added that on an international comparison Borsodchem is expnesive and "it may well be the subject of profit taking as investors in Hungary reposition themselves into stocks with more attractive valuations or less cyclical earnings."
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Borsodchem shares closed at 7,860 forints, down 90.
